stem: In the equation \(p(x + 3) - 2x = 4x + q\), \(p\) and \(q\) are constants. If the equation has infinitely many solutions, what is the value of \(p + q\)?
solution: Infinitely many solutions means both sides are identical: \(p - 2 = 4\) and \(3p = q\).
verify:
x, p, q = symbols('x p q')
d = expand(p*(x + 3) - 2*x - (4*x + q))
sol = solve([d.coeff(x, 1), d.coeff(x, 0)], [p, q], dict=True)
assert len(sol) == 1
s = sol[0][p] + sol[0][q]
assert s == 24
assert Rational(spr_answers[0]) == s and len(spr_answers) == 1
